---
title: "Reshaping data: pivot_longer() and pivot_wider() (solutions)"
format: html
---

Teacher version. Chunks run, so `data/gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv` must exist.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
gapminder_wide <- read_csv(here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv"))
```

## One row per country, one column per year

```{r}
#| label: look-wide
gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`, `2023`)
```

## Your turn 1: plot the wide table

Answer: no column holds the years. They are the names of 301 columns, so `x` has nothing to map to.

## Wide to long: pivot_longer()

```{r}
#| label: make-long
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  )

gapminder_long
```

Answer: 222 rows (3 countries, 74 years) and 3 columns. Without `select()`, `pivot_longer()` keeps `geo` and the other 227 year columns as identifiers. `names_to = "year"` avoids the default `name`, which clashes with the existing `name` column.

## Your turn 2: plot the long table

```{r}
#| label: turn-2
gapminder_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

Answer: the plot is empty and ggplot2 prints `Each group consists of only one observation`. `year` is text, so every point is its own group.

```{r}
#| label: look-long
gapminder_long |>
  glimpse()
```

Answer: `year` is `<chr>`.

## Your turn 3: change the type of year

```{r}
#| label: turn-3
gapminder_long |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

Answer: `as.integer()`. It is a base R function. `as_integer()` does not exist in the tidyverse and returns `could not find function`.

```{r}
#| label: make-long-fixed
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))
```

## Long to wide: pivot_wider()

```{r}
#| label: table2-example
table2 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = count)
```

Answer: 12 rows become 6 rows, with the columns `country`, `year`, `cases` and `population`.

## Your turn 4: back to wide

```{r}
#| label: turn-4
gapminder_long |>
  filter(year %in% c(1990, 2023)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = life_exp) |>
  mutate(change = `2023` - `1990`)
```

Answer: Estonia gained the most, 8.7 years (70.0 in 1990 and 78.7 in 2023). Latvia gained 5.9 years and Lithuania 5.7 years.

## Notes for the teacher

- Column names that start with a digit need backticks, in `select()`, `cols` and `mutate()`.
- `names_transform = as.integer` inside `pivot_longer()` does the type change in one step. This class uses `mutate()` first so that students see the problem.
- If time runs short, Your turn 4 becomes homework.
